newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY LEAGUE-WORLD CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP DATES SHIFTED.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-WORLD CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP DATES SHIFTED.

text.p: The final of rugby league's inaugural world club championship has been put back a week to October 18 because of fixture congestion in both Europe and Australia.

Extra premiership play-offs involving top English clubs in September and a scheduled clash with the test between Australia against New Zealand on September 26 have prompted officials to make the switch.
The world club championship play-offs will now start with quarter-finals on the weekend of October 4-5, followed by semifinals on the following weekend.
The pool stages of the competition, which involves Super League sides from both hemispheres, will take place between June and August during two breaks in the domestic season.
The European Super League kicks off on Friday March 14 when Bradford Bulls face the Warrington Wolves. Super League in Australia made its delayed debut last weekend.
